quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue was $1.786 billion, up 9% sequentially and 6% year over year, with revenue and non-IFRS profitability at or above the high end of guidance. GF shipped approximately 625,000 300-millimeter equivalent wafers, up 8% sequentially and 8% year over year. Gross profit was $534 million for a 29.9% gross margin, above the high end of guidance and up 470 basis points year over year - a second-quarter record that reached the ~30% target well before the end of 2026. Operating profit was $298 million (16.7% margin, +140bps), net income $256 million and diluted EPS $0.46 on ~556 million shares. Manufacturing services were ~89% of revenue and technology services ~11%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $1.786B (+9% QoQ, +6% YoY); gross margin 29.9% (+470bps YoY); operating margin 16.7%; EPS $0.46; ~625k 300mm-equivalent wafers

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue of $1.885 billion plus or minus $25 million; gross margin approximately 30.5% plus or minus 100 basis points (about 450 basis points of year-over-year expansion at the midpoint); operating expenses excluding share-based compensation of $260 million plus or minus $10 million; operating margin 16.7% plus or minus 170 basis points; diluted EPS $0.51 plus or minus $0.05. Full-year 2026 gross margin is now expected at about 30 points for the whole year rather than only as an exit rate, and management reaffirmed the path to a 40% exit run rate in the 2028 timeframe. Full-year adjusted free cash flow margin is still expected at approximately 10%, with capex at the higher end of the 15-20% of revenue range.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $1.885B ±$25M; GM ~30.5% ±100bps; EPS $0.51 ±$0.05; FY2026 GM ~30%; 40% GM exit run rate targeted in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Communications infrastructure and data center was approximately 16% of Q2 revenue and grew 20% sequentially and 62% year over year - the seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth and the fastest quarterly year-on-year growth since 2022. Full-year 2026 growth for the end market was RAISED to 50-60% from a prior expectation of high-30s percent. The implied exit rate is roughly $350 million per quarter, and management reaffirmed the long-term model of 30-plus percent year-over-year growth for this end market into 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: CID ~16% of Q2 revenue, +20% QoQ, +62% YoY; FY2026 growth raised to 50-60% (from high-30s); ~$350M/quarter exit rate

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics revenue reported within comms infrastructure and data center is now expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE in 2026 versus the prior year. GF secured 7 new optical networking design wins in Q2 across both pluggable transceiver suppliers and major hyperscaler and networking players, and is actively engaged with 4 OF THE TOP 5 optical transceiver players. Pluggables contribute the vast majority of silicon photonics revenue today. High-volume manufacturing of 200-gig-per-lane technology is underway, 400-gig capability has already been demonstrated, and the multiyear roadmap advances module enablement to 1.6T, 3.2T and beyond. GF has more than 40 silicon photonics customers, and CEO Tim Breen said GF is on track and potentially ahead of the growth targets set for end-2028 through 2030. He also cited an expectation that 70% of data center links will be optical by 2030, calling that 'perhaps even conservative' given scale-up as well as scale-out penetration.
quarterly_data.figure: Silicon photonics revenue to more than double in 2026; 7 new design wins in Q2; engaged with 4 of top 5 transceiver players; >40 SiPho customers; 200G/lane in HVM, 400G/lane demonstrated

quarterly_data.signal: SCALE, described as the industry's first OCI MSA compatible solution for near and co-packaged optics, has 7 ACTIVE ENGAGEMENTS with leading companies. GF taped out a SCALE-related design win in Q2 and expects to tape out another in Q3. Management reiterated a consistent timeline: the NPO ramp BEGINS IN 2027 and the CPO ramp BEGINS IN 2028. Because near and co-packaged optics are built on a common photonic IC - an EIC bonded to a PIC with a micro-optic and a fiber-attached unit - and differ mainly in that NPO is bonded to the board while CPO sits within the package (plus SerDes architecture differences), GF expects to benefit regardless of which form factor customers adopt. Many customers are pursuing both, with NPO ramping sooner. Breen attributed the sudden industry interest in NPO to SerDes synergies that make the system transition smaller than a jump straight to full CPO, and expects pluggables, NPO and CPO all to coexist in the data center.
quarterly_data.figure: 7 active SCALE engagements; 1 SCALE tape-out in Q2 and another expected in Q3; NPO ramp begins 2027, CPO ramp begins 2028

quarterly_data.signal: GF entered a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for a $300 MILLION award to accelerate next-generation silicon photonics technologies in the U.S. The funding supports three components: continued PIC-level innovation and improved modulator technology to reach 400-gig per lane and beyond; NEW MATERIALS to be introduced into the system - management named barium titanate, thin-film lithium niobate and indium phosphide; and packaging capability and capacity for the integrated optical engines needed for near and co-packaged optics, building directly on the SCALE platform. Management said the endorsement came from the world's top XPU providers, hyperscalers, AI connectivity leaders and ecosystem partners.
quarterly_data.figure: $300M U.S. Department of Commerce letter of intent for next-generation silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon germanium is OVERSUBSCRIBED THROUGHOUT 2027 and, notably, GF's SiGe business is LARGER THAN ITS SILICON PHOTONICS BUSINESS TODAY. GF secured multiple new SiGe TIA and driver design wins across networking customers in the quarter. The growth has two compounding drivers: the shift to optical networking itself, and the fact that what could previously be done in CMOS at 50-gig and 100-gig per lane cannot be done at 200-gig and definitely not at 400-gig per lane, forcing transimpedance amplifiers and increasingly the drivers out into high-performance analog processes like SiGe. High-performance analog also appears in near and co-packaged optics depending on architecture. GF is expanding SiGe capacity at Burlington, Vermont and qualifying 300-millimeter SiGe in Singapore for additional capacity, better economics and higher fT/fMAX performance. The SiGe lineage traces to IBM Microelectronics, which invented SiGe and is part of GF today.
quarterly_data.figure: SiGe oversubscribed throughout 2027; SiGe business larger than silicon photonics today; Vermont capacity expanding, 300mm SiGe qualifying in Singapore

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity strategy is a structural advantage: GF is adding capacity WITHIN ITS EXISTING FAB FOOTPRINT rather than building new fabs, which management contrasted with competitors on longer lead times. Breen said GF 'could 10x our photonics capacity within our current 4 walls' globally on its long-term plan. Q2 utilization was in the high 80s, leaving about 10 points of headroom to grow into with installed capacity. Confidence in bringing capacity online plus factory productivity improvements was cited as a direct contributor to raising the full-year CID outlook. On competition in silicon photonics, Breen said customers are coming to GF saying they do not have enough capacity secured and want more, partly to mitigate geopolitical risk, and he sees no customer-concentration concern given 40-plus customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Photonics capacity expandable ~10x within existing fabs; Q2 utilization high-80s with ~10 points of headroom

quarterly_data.signal: GF implemented PRICING INCREASES in partnership with customers across several technology corridors during Q2, following what management called constructive conversations. The adjustments will be reflected in revenue COMMENCING IN 2027, with magnitude varying by end market and technology based on differentiated value, supply/demand dynamics and inflationary absorption. GF will continue assessing 2027 pricing through the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Price increases agreed across several technology corridors, revenue impact commencing 2027

quarterly_data.signal: GF launched Quantum Technology Solutions in May 2026, a dedicated team aimed at taking the quantum industry from prototypes to high-volume production. The strategy is qubit-agnostic across superconducting, trapped ion, photonic, topological and spin modalities, using the FDX platform as a cryogenic CMOS foundation and extending advanced packaging into the cryogenic regime for 3D heterogeneous integration. GF is working with 8 of the world's leading quantum computing players including PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Quantum Motion plus endorsements from the quantum arms of large hyperscalers, and has already begun 4 new customer-specific engagements in the three months since launch. The effort is anchored by an expected $375 MILLION grant from the U.S. Department of Commerce. Over the next 1 to 3 years quantum revenue comes largely through engineering engagements booked in technology services, with manufacturing-services revenue ramping toward the end of the decade. Several quantum players are working on the photonics side of their solutions, which maps directly onto GF's silicon photonics roadmap.
quarterly_data.figure: $375M expected U.S. Department of Commerce quantum grant; 8 leading quantum players engaged; 4 new customer engagements in 3 months

quarterly_data.signal: IP, software and custom silicon: GF completed the acquisition of the Synopsys ARC processor IP Solutions business in June, adding CPU, DSP, NPU and RISC-V technologies, a software development toolkit and application-specific processor design capability - over 150 patents, 300 existing customers and 400 R&D engineers. Combined with MIPS, this lets GF engage customers earlier in the design cycle for edge AI and on-device inference in automotive, industrial and robotics. Full-year 2026 technology services contribution from MIPS plus ARC was RAISED to $100-120 million from a prior $60-100 million, skewed roughly one third Q3 and two thirds Q4, and technology services revenue is now expected toward the high end of the 10-12% of total revenue range with gross margin significantly above corporate targets. Design wins in the quarter included 3 strategic chiplet wins with Lockheed Martin on FinFET and FDX, an expanded FinFET win with Microchip, a first-ever PMIC design win with MediaTek on the BCD platform, an ADAS radar tape-out for Bosch on FDX, and a new microLED display backplane win for augmented reality wearables at a leading hyperscaler.
quarterly_data.figure: Technology services contribution raised to $100M-$120M for 2026 (from $60M-$100M); ARC adds 150 patents, 300 customers, 400 R&D engineers

quarterly_data.signal: End-market split and the memory-shortage read-across: smart mobile devices were ~36% of Q2 revenue, up 15% sequentially but down 6% year over year, and are now expected to DECLINE BY A LOW-TEENS PERCENTAGE in 2026 because 2026 handset forecasts have been cut meaningfully on continued memory pricing and associated shortages. Automotive was ~19% of revenue, down 13% sequentially and 10% year over year on customer-led shipment timing, but full-year low-double-digit growth is still expected weighted to Q4. Home and industrial IoT was ~19% of revenue, up 30% sequentially and 10% year over year - its fastest year-over-year growth since 2022 - and the full-year outlook was raised to 10-15% growth from mid-single digits, partly because mobile customers reallocated demand into IoT connectivity applications. GF credited a deliberately flexible manufacturing footprint for reusing capacity to capture data-center upside as mobile weakened.
quarterly_data.figure: Smart mobile ~36% of revenue, FY2026 down low teens on memory shortage; automotive ~19%; IoT ~19%, FY2026 raised to 10-15% growth

quarterly_data.signal: Cash and capital returns: Q2 cash flow from operations was $405 million and capex net of government grant proceeds was $408 million (roughly 23% of revenue), leaving adjusted free cash flow at negative $3 million as previously guided. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $3.3 billion against $1.1 billion of total debt, with a $1 billion revolving credit facility undrawn. GF paid its first-ever quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share on July 14 and declared another $0.12 per share payable October 9, 2026. Approximately $100 million remains under the share repurchase authorization; the stated objective is to return up to 50% of trailing-twelve-month non-IFRS adjusted free cash flow after investments over time.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 OCF $405M; capex $408M (~23% of revenue); adjusted FCF -$3M; $3.3B cash and securities; first-ever dividend $0.12/share

quarterly_data.signal: Data center power is GF's third named growth pillar alongside silicon photonics and SiGe. In July GF closed a strategic acquihire of the custom power team from Photon Technologies in Europe, bringing an experienced design team focused on INTEGRATED VOLTAGE REGULATORS (IVRs). Combined with GF's BCD, GaN and integrated-inductor capabilities, the goal is a new power architecture that brings power conversion closer to the processor to meet the efficiency, power density, bandwidth, high-current and transient-response requirements of next-generation XPUs. CEO Tim Breen framed it directly: 'IVR is to power what CPO is to photonics' - moving from traditional industrial/automotive-style power modules to a much more wafer-level integrated solution delivering power closer to the chip. The Photon team is already engaged with a number of existing GF customers, and early feedback from fabless companies, IDMs and hyperscalers has been very positive.

GF closed a first-of-a-kind design win for SMART POWER STAGE GATE DRIVERS on its BCD platform for data center power applications, which management called one notable step into a rapidly evolving market. The quarter also brought a significant automotive power design win for 5-volt and 10-volt power management integrated circuits on BCD, and a first-ever PMIC design win with long-standing customer MediaTek on the same platform - evidence that the BCD power platform is expanding across data center, automotive and mobile.
quarterly_data.figure: First-of-a-kind smart power stage gate driver design win on BCD; automotive 5V/10V PMIC win; first-ever MediaTek PMIC win
